x-bump-note: 2.3.0 -> 2.4.0 (reaped-from-session-declaration) declares the optional top-level string `reaped_from_session`, the archived twin of the same declaration landing on handoff.schema.json 6.0.0 -> 6.1.0 in this same commit — see that file's note for the full rationale and the sender's memo. Classified nested-field-additive on the same grounds: a new optional top-level scalar, no domain narrowed, no archived document invalidated. Declared here even though claude-klabauter-em explicitly asserted nothing about this file, because the two questions are not the same one: they were right to revert a BACKFILL that wrote the key onto archived records (that asserts a conclusion about an archived document), and declaring the key asserts no such conclusion — the archival path carries frontmatter through wholesale, so a live carrier archives carrying it, and leaving it undeclared here rebuilds the undeclared-on-disk state one archival sweep later. Sits beside the claim vocabulary (consumed_by/consumed_at/claimed_by/claimed_at) this schema already declares. PRIOR: 2.2.0 -> 2.3.0 (baton-kind-vocabulary-one-axis-per-field C10) WIDENED the `kind` enum to admit the new D1 target names (`roadmap-baton`, `goal-seed`, `roadmap-seed`) landing on the live handoff.schema.json's own C10 narrow, retaining every retired name (`spinoff-roadmap`, `spinoff-goal`, `spinoff-roadmap-creator`) alongside them rather than swapping — this schema's whole reason for being more permissive than the live schema is that the archived corpus permanently retains historical kind values, exactly as it already does for `spike-result` and for `consumed`/`superseded` on `status` above. Classified nested-field-additive (widening an existing field's enum domain, never rejects a previously-valid document) — not major, since narrowing is the semantics-changed case that classification exists for, and this bump is the strict inverse of that. 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 declared the optional `shipped_in_kind` discriminant (DR-096, closed enum ship-commit|successor|scope-derived|no-commit, parity with handoff.schema.json), with NO cross-field enforcement — unlike the live schema this record is purely additive since archived batons are grandfathered per DR-096 § Census, never migrated. Prior bump 2.0.0 -> 2.1.0 added the optional top-level `disposed_successors` array (reverse-pointing lineage edges, parity with handoff.schema.json).
description: Archived handoff — relaxed-schema sibling of handoff for already-consumed handoffs archived by /pickup. deployment_state and gate_dependency are not required; cross-field rules from handoff do not apply. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-05-08-roadmap-skill-and-handoff-lifecycle.md § Phase 1b

branch.description: Git branch this handoff was created on.

status.description: 'superseded' is retired (2026-06-26) but retained here for archived/legacy/sibling read-tolerance — the archived corpus (archive/handoffs/) still holds records written under the retired vocabulary and this schema must keep reading them. (Retracted 2026-07-22: no emit path validates against this schema pre-coerce — example-doctrine-repo's emit-cockpit-snapshot.py is a fail-loud stub with no validation body, and claude-klabauter's records-query emit path reads handoffs without schema validation, coercing old→new vocabulary afterwards in Python. Do not re-derive an emit-narrowing constraint from this description.) DR-084 P4 narrow landed 2026-07-22 removing 'active'/'consumed' from this enum on the verified premise of a clean example-doctrine-repo corpus. Restored 2026-07-27: this schema is the fleet-shared reader validator for sibling repos' archived corpora too, and claude-klabauter's archive/handoffs/ holds 11 records written under the retired 'consumed' vocabulary — 'consumed' is restored here on exactly the read-tolerance grounds that retain 'superseded' above. 'active' remains retired — no record in any surveyed corpus carries it; restore it only on corpus evidence. The live handoff.schema.json keeps its narrow ['open','claimed'] and is unaffected by this restoration.

predecessor.description: Predecessor handoff path, or null for spinoffs. Key must be present (string-or-null: D9).

consumed_by.description: Session id of the consuming /pickup invocation; sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.

consumed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was consumed. Permissive: archive corpus mixes legacy bare-date and current date-time (reader-tolerate).

claimed_by.description: Session id of the claiming /pickup invocation (DR-084 successor of consumed_by; new-vocabulary records use this). Sourced from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with .current-session-id fallback. Cross-field rule (claimed + claimed_at ⇒ claimed_by required) lands at P4.

claimed_at.description: Timestamp when the handoff was claimed (ISO 8601 date-time; DR-084 successor of consumed_at). Stamped by the claim transition for race-forensics precision.

reaped_from_session.description: Session id of the DEAD holder whose claim a crash-orphan reaper released before this record archived — see handoff.schema.json's twin for the full write-site semantics. Declared here because the archival path carries frontmatter through wholesale, so a live record carrying the key archives carrying it; declaring it is not a claim that the reaped work completed, only that the strip happened while the record was live.

shipped_in.description: DR-096: names the ship commit — the caller-supplied commit SHA at which this baton was declared shipped (DR-096 meaning 2), or a plan path / the substantively-shipped-no-commit token on legacy archived records. See shipped_in_kind for the discriminant tagging which of the four DR-096 write-time shapes produced this value (declared here, not enforced — this archived schema's cross-field rules from handoff do not apply).

shipped_in_kind.description: Archived-handoff sibling of the live handoff.shipped_in_kind discriminant — see that field's description for the four values' meanings. Not required here (this object enforces no cross-field rules), backfilled where known; absent on records archived before the discriminant existed.

continued_into.description: Successor pointer for deployment_state=continued — handoff_id (hnd-<slug>-<6hex>) preferred, state/handoffs/... path fallback (pre-existing successors carry no handoff_id; no backfill). The tooth that keeps 'continued' from becoming liveness-guess abandonment: an automated writer that cannot name the successor cannot stamp continued. Required-when-continued (landed at the P4 narrow, 2026-07-22).

disposed_successors.description: Lineage-preservation edges written by distill.apply_disposal (C14) BEFORE a successor handoff is deleted: each entry is a successor's continued-into value (handoff_id preferred, path fallback — same shape as continued_into) for a successor that continued this record's work and was later disposed by /distill. Multi-valued (unlike continued_into, single-valued and deployment_state=continued-gated) because a parent can accumulate multiple disposed successors across separate /distill runs; each entry is append-only and never overwritten. Distinct from continued_into: this field is NOT deployment_state-conditional and is NOT itself the successor pointer for this record's own lifecycle — it is a reverse-pointing lineage record of OTHER records that pointed at this one and have since been deleted. Declared here as well as in handoff.schema.json because archival is exactly when the field earns its keep: the disposed successor is gone, and the archived parent is the only surviving record of the edge.

closed_reason.description: Deliberate-stop subtype for deployment_state=closed (human/session only, never automated — DR-084). cancelled = deliberate stop; displaced = replaced with NO lineage edge (with an edge it's continued, not closed); stale = overtaken by events. Deliberately NO crashed/orphaned value: a successor-less dead-holder has no automated terminal — it surfaces for adjudication. Required-when-closed (landed at the P4 narrow, 2026-07-22).

machine.description: Machine identifier where the session ran.

kind.description: Kind of handoff. Synced to the live handoff.schema.json enum (2026-07-07 sister fork kinds spinoff-goal/spinoff-roadmap-creator; 2026-07-21 spike-result per DEC-3a) — archived records may carry any live kind, so this sibling schema must not drift narrower than the source. WIDENED, never narrowed (baton-kind-vocabulary-one-axis-per-field C10): the live schema's C10 bump RETIRED spinoff-roadmap/spinoff-goal/spinoff-roadmap-creator in favor of roadmap-baton/goal-seed/roadmap-seed, but this archived sibling ADDS the new names alongside the old ones rather than swapping — the archived corpus permanently retains every historical kind value a record was ever written under, exactly as this schema already does for the retired 'consumed'/'superseded' status values and the retired 'spike-result' kind above. Narrowing this enum would invalidate already-archived records written under the pre-C10 vocabulary.

authoring_session.description: Session id that authored this handoff. On kind: session-handoff, coordinator-doc-new's scaffolder stamps this machine-generated at scaffold time (omitted, not PLACEHOLDER, when no session id is resolvable) -- coordinator_core.baton_assemble's cross-authorship adoption predicate (_adopt_prior_attempt_scaffold_path) gates adoption of a prior attempt's scaffold on this field matching the resuming run's own session id.

pickup_ready.description: Positive pickup-authorized signal; preserved verbatim from the active schema on archival.

deployment_state.description: Deployment state at time of archival. DR-084 P4 narrow landed 2026-07-22: 'abandoned' retired; 'continued' and 'closed' are its replacements.

gate_dependency.description: Gate dependency condition (only relevant when deployment_state=awaiting_gate).

blocks.description: List of handoff IDs this handoff blocks.

blocked_by.description: List of handoff IDs that block this handoff.

roadmap_id.description: Roadmap identifier for spinoff-roadmap kind handoffs.

reviewed_at_workstream_complete.description: Review marker: '<sha-range> <reviewer> <YYYY-MM-DD>'. Written by /workstream-complete and /handoff after running coordinator:review-code. Absent on spinoff-kind handoffs.

provision_eta.description: Optional advisory ETA for a downstream install-leg's provisioning step (e.g. indexing the operator's own project) — free-text estimate, not a gate. Seen on install-leg spinoff batons (e.g. archive/handoffs/install-example-retrieval-repo.md, archive/handoffs/install-example-retrieval-repo-ue-addon.md). Backfilled into the schema at C6 GAP3 (was previously undeclared but permissively valid — no additionalProperties: false on this schema).

handoff_id.description: Durable stable ID for this handoff/spinoff record, path-independent (survives archival move/rename). OPTIONAL — pre-existing handoffs authored before this field was introduced carry no handoff_id and are NOT backfilled. Backfilled into this archived schema per its declare-every-field convention (C2, review integrator, 2026-07-08).

predecessor_id.description: ID-companion for predecessor (C2, add-not-swap) — the predecessor's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME predecessor the path field names. Null when the predecessor has no handoff_id or predecessor is none/null. Backfilled into this archived schema per its declare-every-field convention (C2, review integrator, 2026-07-08). Widened to anyOf[string,null] (2026-07-17) to match the live handoff.schema.json shape and its own documented null case — the plain 'type: string' declaration rejected the documented null value.

origin_handoff_id.description: ID-companion for origin_handoff (C2, add-not-swap) — the originating baton's handoff_id, resolved and stamped at author time from the SAME baton origin_handoff names. Null when the originating baton has no handoff_id or origin_handoff is null. Backfilled into this archived schema per its declare-every-field convention (C2, review integrator, 2026-07-08). Widened to anyOf[string,null] (2026-07-27) to match the live handoff.schema.json shape and its own documented null case — the plain 'type: string' declaration rejected the documented null value.
